contracts.native_physical_ABI: ECX receiver; incoming EDX unconsumed and overwritten by the initial begin load; one stacked fill-header address; both exits RET 4. Direct receiver fields are begin +4, end +8, capacity +C. No direct +0 access; admitted aliases may still affect those bytes.
contracts.initial_reads: Capture initial begin first. If zero, size becomes zero without an initial end read, and capacity is not read. Otherwise load initial end, compute SAR4 of wrapped end-minus-begin, then load capacity and compute SAR4 of wrapped capacity-minus-begin. The spare comparison is unsigned.
contracts.spare_path: Capture current end after the two native fill-argument loads. Call actual 00698040 with output=captured end, count=1, source=fill, owner bits=receiver, value bits=fill, and native partially initialized tag bits. On successful return publish captured end+0x10 to receiver+8; never recompute current end and never use child EAX.
contracts.spare_null_output: Do not guard captured end==0. The actual counted-fill core skips source/header access and construction on null output, still advances/publishes its cursor, and Append stores captured end+0x10.
contracts.partial_native_tag: The original only zeroes the low byte of its local DWORD before pushing the entire word. Its high 24 bits are unspecified. Complete accepted normal/catch/action proof shows core slots 3 and 4 are unconsumed. A future Source call may use canonical unused tag 0 while explicitly declining native high-bit/frame identity; it must not read an uninitialized C++ DWORD or claim the native word was zero.
contracts.owner_bits: Pass receiver bits as observed. Core reads owner only for a nonempty prefix catch and forwards it to actual 004D29D0, whose accepted implementation ignores that owner context.
contracts.slow_path: Capture current end into EDI. Compare captured initial begin against captured end; if initial begin is greater call returning 00BF6713. Retain captured EDI across that service, then read the fill argument and call actual 006988F0(receiver, canonical unused EDX 0, private output pair, receiver, captured end, fill). No subsequent current-end position reload.
contracts.private_output: Reserve two private 4-byte words for the actual InsertOne output; do not invent an iterator object or ownership. InsertOne result and both output words are ignored by Append. Native argument/frame aliases and register/flag identity remain outside the new Source interface.
contracts.return: No stable semantic EAX. The fast path retains incidental core residue; the slow path retains a pointer to the private output pair. The sole bounded caller immediately overwrites EAX. A future Source interface returns void.
contracts.arithmetic: All public-address arithmetic wraps in uint32_t, with explicit arithmetic-right-shift bit semantics. No typed-array subtraction, count bridge, endpoint validation, whole-header snapshot, or extra null guard.

ownership_and_failure: Fast child failure propagates without the Append end publication; the child owns its constructor and completed-prefix cleanup. Existing public alias effects remain; Append performs no rollback.
Fast success publishes the captured original output+0x10 after the child returns, even if child aliases changed current receiver fields.
A throwing slow-path diagnostic prevents InsertOne; a returning diagnostic preserves captured initial begin and captured end while any public handler effects remain.
Slow InsertOne failure propagates its actual progress; the private output pair owns no resources and adds no cleanup.
Append itself has no local catch, unwind action, fill ownership, or noexcept bridge. Transitive child cleanup is not caller EH.
